findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the reference timestamp for the clean_close cutoff (e.g. a build_time field returned by build_corpus, or the max event timestamp in the corpus) so the label is deterministic for a fixed content_hash.
evidence: 'clean_close (closed, no escape signals, closed ≥CLEAN_CLOSE_MIN_DAYS days before the corpus build — named constant, default 7)'
corpus.build_corpus is described as returning manifest["content_hash"] but no build-timestamp field is named
findings.finding: The clean_close label depends on 'closed ≥ CLEAN_CLOSE_MIN_DAYS days before the corpus build', but the plan never states the provenance of the 'corpus build' reference time — whether it is a timestamp carried in build_corpus's manifest, wall-clock now(), or a caller-supplied value. Without a stated source the day-arithmetic is unreproducible and the label is non-deterministic across runs.
scenarios: Re-running labels.py the next day flips a clean_close label because 'now' advanced past the threshold, changing report counts against the same content_hash
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the reference time from the corpus itself (e.g. the latest event timestamp in the manifest) rather than wall-clock now(), and record it in the report alongside content_hash.

findings.checklist_item: Correct the caused_by direction: it is stored OUTBOUND on the bug (in deps) and appears INBOUND only on the origin; specify which ticket escaped_defect labels and read the correct edge (bug's deps for a caused_by target, or the origin's inbound_deps), not the bug's inbound_deps.
evidence: Plan: "and include_inbound=True so caused_by (an INBOUND link onto a bug) is present in inbound_deps"
Plan: "escaped_defect = UNION of (close_class == 'plan_defect' on the ticket's own state) OR (an inbound caused_by link is present in inbound_deps)"

reads.py:324-334 inbound_deps_state: 'A LINK event is stored one-sided on the SOURCE ticket's record, so a ticket's own deps list carries only its OUTGOING edges'; each inbound entry means 'from_id <relation> this ticket'
tests/unit/test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py:47-49 reads caused_by from show_ticket(bug)['deps'] (outbound on the bug); rebar.link(bug, origin, 'caused_by') draws bug->origin
findings.finding: The plan's directional claim about caused_by is refuted by the store's link model: it states caused_by is 'an INBOUND link onto a bug ... present in inbound_deps' and makes escaped_defect's second disjunct fire when 'an inbound caused_by link is present in inbound_deps' (read via show_ticket on the ticket with include_inbound=True). But a caused_by LINK is stored one-sided on the SOURCE ticket (the bug) and is drawn bug->origin (rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by). So the BUG carries caused_by as an OUTBOUND edge in its own deps, and only the ORIGIN/culprit ticket carries it INBOUND in inbound_deps. include_inbound=True on the bug will never surface its caused_by edge; the escaped_defect inbound-caused_by disjunct silently never fires on the bug, and if evaluated on the origin it labels a different ticket set than close_class=='plan_defect' (which is on the bug).
findings.location: Approach → 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, corrected units)' and 'Ticket-level labels' (escaped_defect); Context paragraph 3
scenarios: Every plan_defect bug: escaped_defect fires only via close_class, never via the caused_by disjunct — 89 caused_by-linked outcomes are dropped or mis-attached
AC 'labels report counts matching independent jq counts ... for caused_by' fails because the label reads the wrong edge direction
findings.suggested_fix: State that caused_by is drawn bug->origin (one-sided on the bug per reads.py:324). If escaped_defect labels the bug, read caused_by from the bug's OUTBOUND deps (include_inbound not required for it). If it labels the culprit/origin, read the origin's inbound_deps for a caused_by entry — and reconcile that this is a different ticket than close_class=='plan_defect', which sits on the bug.

findings.finding: The Approach mislabels the caused_by edge direction: it calls caused_by 'an INBOUND link onto a bug' present in the bug's inbound_deps, but the edge is stored OUTBOUND on the bug (source) pointing to the culprit (target); it is INBOUND only on the CULPRIT ticket.
findings.location: Approach, 'Ticket-level event source (multi-store, corrected units)' bullet and 'Ticket-level labels' bullet (escaped_defect)
scenarios: Implementer reads inbound_deps of a BUG expecting caused_by and finds none (it is outbound on the bug), so escaped_defect never fires via the caused_by branch.
Or the escaped_defect subject is intended to be the culprit ticket, but the 'onto a bug' phrasing sends the implementer to the wrong endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'caused_by is a directional edge stored on the bug's outbound deps (bug -> culprit); on the CULPRIT ticket it is INBOUND. escaped_defect fires for a ticket that is the target of a bug's caused_by edge — read via show_ticket(culprit, include_inbound=True).inbound_deps filtered to relation == "caused_by".'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix escaped_defect's caused_by source: read the caused_by edge from the bug's OUTBOUND deps (not inbound_deps), and state explicitly whether escaped_defect labels the bug (deps caused_by + own plan_defect) or the culprit (inbound_deps caused_by from_id=<bug>), since plan_defect and caused_by-outbound both attach to the bug while caused_by-inbound attaches to the culprit.

Plan: 'escaped_defect = UNION of (close_class == "plan_defect" on the ticket's own state) OR (an inbound caused_by link is present in inbound_deps)'

reads.py:321-341 inbound_deps_state returns edges where OTHER tickets link TO the subject, each {from_id, relation, status}; a bug that IS the caused_by source has no such inbound entry for its own caused_by edge
Context lists both plan_defect (84) and caused_by (89) as BUG-level outcome signals, so escaped_defect's subject is the bug — where caused_by is outbound
findings.finding: escaped_defect's caused_by half reads the wrong edge list: a caused_by link is stored on the SOURCE bug's OUTBOUND deps, not its inbound_deps, so checking inbound_deps on the bug (the same ticket that carries close_class=plan_defect) yields nothing and the signal is silently always-false.
findings.location: Approach → 'Ticket-level event source' and 'Ticket-level labels' (escaped_defect); Context para 3
scenarios: Any bug closed with close_class=plan_defect AND a caused_by edge to its culprit: escaped_defect fires only on the plan_defect half; the caused_by half never contributes, so the 89-count caused_by signal the ticket was written to exploit is lost
A bug that has ONLY a caused_by link (no plan_defect close_class) is mislabelled clean_close/non-escaped
findings.suggested_fix: For a bug-subject escaped_defect, join `close_class == "plan_defect"` (own state) with a caused_by entry in the ticket's own `deps` (outbound); if the intent is to flag the CULPRIT ticket instead, take caused_by from the culprit's `inbound_deps` (from_id=bug) and drop plan_defect from the culprit's own-state test (it lives on the bug). Either way, include_inbound=True is only needed for the culprit-subject variant.

findings.checklist_item: Define how the per-question agreement metric traverses the nested `verification` block ({binary, severity_attributes}) down to individual sub-answer keys, and specify the rule when the two reviews' sub-group/key sets differ (which keys count toward the pooled denominator).
evidence: Plan: 'for each `norm_id` present in BOTH reviews of a pair with a `verification` dict in both, compare each shared sub-answer key's value ... (# key-comparisons where old value == new value) / (total key-comparisons)'
sidecar.py:687 persists `"verification": f.get("verification")` — the full nested block

Fixtures confirm the shape is two-level: tests/unit/test_sidecar_enrichment.py:58 `"verification": {"binary": {}, "severity_attributes": {}}`; test_code_review_fp_ledger.py:321 `{"binary": {"is_real": "yes"}, "severity_attributes": {"blast": "narrow"}}`

A naive flat-dict comparison would compare the sub-DICTS ('binary' vs 'binary') by object equality, not the individual is_real/blast sub-answers the metric intends — silently mis-computing the pooled agreement denominator and value.
findings.finding: The per-question Pass-2 agreement metric treats the `verification` dict as a flat {key: value} map, but the persisted verification is a NESTED dict ({"binary": {k: v}, "severity_attributes": {k: v}}); the plan never defines how to traverse the nesting to enumerate 'sub-answer key's value' comparisons.
findings.location: Approach → 'Noise floor', bullet (c) per-question Pass-2 agreement
scenarios: An identical-material pair whose two reviews each carry `verification={"binary":{...},"severity_attributes":{...}}` — the metric must descend into both groups to compare `is_real`, `blast`, etc., not compare the two group dicts.
Two reviews whose verification dicts have differing sub-group keys (e.g. one has severity_attributes, the other does not).
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that key-comparisons are enumerated over the union/intersection of leaf sub-answer keys within EACH known group (binary, severity_attributes), pooling only keys present in both reviews' same group; state whether keys present in one review but not the other are excluded from or counted as a disagreement in the denominator.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify per-store/per-ticket read-failure behavior: define whether a ticket absent from a store or a failing show_ticket for one store aborts the build or is surfaced (logged/counted) rather than silently dropped.
evidence: Plan: 'for each store_name, tracker_git_root in store_roots, call show_ticket(ticket_id, repo_root=str(Path(tracker_git_root).parent), include_inbound=True)'

The plan specifies explicit raises for hash-mismatch and store-name-mismatch, but is silent on a ticket missing from a store or show_ticket failing on one store of several — a real failure point in a multi-store read loop.
ABSENCE: no stated retry/skip/surface policy for a per-store read failure; error states for this path are neither surfaced-explicitly nor documented as safe to swallow.
findings.finding: The multi-store ticket-label path calls show_ticket(ticket_id, repo_root=<parent>) once per store and reuses a per-store git-walk, but the plan does not state behavior when a ticket is absent from a given store or when show_ticket raises for one store while other stores succeed — whether the run aborts, skips, or logs and continues is unspecified.
scenarios: A ticket id present in the local store but not in a second store: show_ticket may raise or return empty, and it is unclear whether the whole labels build fails or that ticket's cross-store signals are silently dropped, changing escaped_defect/reopened counts.
One store's tracker git is transiently unreadable while others succeed: unclear whether the report is emitted with partial (silently incomplete) counts or the run aborts.
findings.suggested_fix: State that a ticket not present in a given store contributes no signals from that store (documented, not an error), and that a store that fails to read (git-walk or show_ticket raises) aborts the build with an error naming the store — so partial counts are never silently published.
